svg.text: ENCOUNTER-001
The adversarial root of “encounter” does not establish an adversarial theory of encounter.
ENCOUNTER-002
Goffman technicalizes encounter by removing surprise and trouble from it.
ENCOUNTER-003
Turing produces the machine encounter by preventing an ordinary encounter.
ENCOUNTER-004
Licklider’s “symbiosis” preserves a division of agency inside the partnership.
ENCOUNTER-005
Direct manipulation succeeds by making the computer disappear as an encountered entity.
ENCOUNTER-006
Suchman makes “human-machine interaction” itself an empirical question.
ENCOUNTER-007
Pratt changes the unit from two encountering subjects to a historically produced contact space.
ENCOUNTER-008
Barad makes encounter potentially too late: interaction already assumes the entities it claims to relate.
ENCOUNTER-009
For Deleuze, encounter is diagnosed by failed recognition, not by reciprocity.
ENCOUNTER-010
Althusser’s encounter is successful only when contingency “takes hold” long enough to make a world.
ENCOUNTER-011
“Interface” converts meeting into a boundary that can be engineered.
ENCOUNTER-AI-012
Floridi’s Encounters is an experiment that contains encounters, not yet a theory of encounter.
ENCOUNTER-AI-013
Distant writing moves authorship from inscription into control of a generative possibility space.
ENCOUNTER-AI-014
Floridi permits artificial agency while refusing artificial intelligence.
ENCOUNTER-AI-015
The AI ethnographic encounter is valuable when it deforms the observer’s categories.
ENCOUNTER-AI-016
Encounter Ontology gives human–AI encounter structural admission criteria.
ENCOUNTER-AI-017
Buberian opposition makes refusal and vulnerability conditions of encounter, not defects to optimize away.
ENCOUNTER-AI-018
Artificial otherness may require a new category rather than a verdict of humanlike or nonhuman.
ENCOUNTER-AI-019
Human–robot research proposed a new ontological category fifteen years before LLM encounter ontology.
ENCOUNTER-AI-020
HCI operationalized long-term human–computer relationship before generative AI made relation appear spontaneous.
ENCOUNTER-AI-021
Before theorizing AI encounter, philosophy must decide whether communication occurred at all.
ENCOUNTER-AI-022
The strongest counterexample to AI-as-other is AI-as-instrument.
ENCOUNTER-AI-023
Language may construct the artificial Other before the machine earns that status ontologically.
ENCOUNTER-OP-024
An encounter needs observable entry, maintenance, and exit conditions before it needs a score.
ENCOUNTER-OP-025
Connection events make relational participation computable without claiming access to inner states.
ENCOUNTER-OP-026
An encounter classifier can be accurate while operationalizing no stable encounter construct.
ENCOUNTER-OP-027
Breakdown exposes reciprocity more clearly than smooth conversation does.
ENCOUNTER-OP-028
Successful repair can conceal that the human is carrying the encounter.
ENCOUNTER-OP-029
The encounter may have to be measured as a trajectory of coordination rather than as properties of either participant.
ENCOUNTER-OP-030
Joint attention to a shared object can be more diagnostic than attention to the artificial partner.
ENCOUNTER-OP-031
Multi-turn generativity becomes analytically useful only when turns co-develop something.
ENCOUNTER-OP-032
Recursion must be separated from being stuck in a loop.
ENCOUNTER-OP-033
Linguistic convergence is measurable but does not prove encounter.
ENCOUNTER-OP-034
An encounter may leave a trace in how the human models the entity on the next turn.
ENCOUNTER-OP-035
Resistance can be manipulated experimentally, but disagreement may make AI seem less socially other.
ENCOUNTER-OP-036
Post-encounter residue becomes measurable when continuity is disrupted.
ENCOUNTER-OP-037
Operational encounter needs admission conditions, process signatures, and after-effects kept separate.
